claims.sentence_start: Busi treats the disclaimer as more a confession
claims.note: Busi 1496-1501: 'Piu che una scusa è una confessione'; the reputation of Pico mago persisted after his death; Benivieni denied it. Note 69 (1558-1559): Benivieni's letter of 15 March 1514. Date checked.

claims.sentence_start: In the Apology Pico made this thesis the anchor of his defence of the rest
claims.note: The Apology passage (quoted in note 16 of the entry CHARACTERES, citing Apologia pp. 168, 176) limits only his conclusions 'de figuris, de numeris': he does not mean their superstitious use by pacts with demons, 'quia hec omnia reprobavi in prima conclusione mea'. It does not make 9>1 the anchor of the defence of 'the rest'.

claims.sentence_start: Busi and Ebgi summarise the Apology's argument
claims.note: Content supported ('magia è termine equivoco ... giustamente è stata bandita dalla Chiesa'), but the passage is in the lexicon entry CHARACTERES (9627-10199), signed [R. E.] at 10199: it is Ebgi's, not Busi's and Ebgi's.

claims.sentence_start: Farmer judges that the magical theses
claims.note: The clause on the magical theses is at farmer1998:1357-1358 ('his magical theses, which, despite all disclaimers, were always open to suspicions of demonology and witch-craft').

claims.sentence_start: Voltaire read the first proposition against its intent
claims.note: Voltaire (Copenhaver's translation) paraphrases the first proposition and infers that Pico would grant that magic is the work of demons, calling the words 'contradictory'. 'Against its intent' is the drafter's judgement, not the source's; 9>1 itself ascribes the condemned magic to the powers of darkness.

claims.sentence_start: Copenhaver cites this passage of the Essai among the jibes
claims.note: Note 29 (23036) cites 'App. C.17.T2M1 ... Voltaire 1963, 2:87-89' and the text says Pico 'hit bottom in Europe's memory'; nothing about 'jibes' or 'a figure of fun'.

claims.sentence_start: Farmer places the thesis within the conventional prologue
claims.note: Farmer's note (on 9>1-2) says only that medieval magical treatises regularly began by protesting that their magic was natural, not demonic; 'a protest of innocence rather than a new doctrine' is not in Farmer.

claims.sentence_start: Copenhaver reads the first four theses as a public strategy
claims.note: Copenhaver asks 'Did Pico want to advertise natural magic while keeping quiet about angel-magic?' and answers that the theses on magic (M) as a whole 'suggest so' (17361-17363). He does not tie the strategy to the first four theses, and he frames it as a question.

claims.sentence_start: Busi reads it as a confession
claims.note: Busi: 'Piu che una scusa è una confessione'; note: 'è l'inizio della prima tra le ventisei Conclusiones magicae secundum opinionem propriam'. 'The suspicion Pico expected' is a light gloss on 'I malevoli lo devono aver pensato già nel 1486'.

claims.sentence_start: The thesis matters for the whole series because
claims.note: The Apology applies 9>1 to his conclusions on figures and numbers, not to 'every magical conclusion that followed'.

claims.sentence_start: Whether the commission examined this thesis at all
claims.note: Copenhaver's Q1-Q13 list has no magic heading; 9>1 is not among the thirteen.
